You reported task 1.3 complete. Before it is integrated, one pass over your own work — the pass a reviewer would otherwise spend a full round on.

These are not open questions. Each has a definite answer and you either found something or you did not:

1. Re-read every comment, docstring, header and test name ADJACENT TO A LINE YOU CHANGED. Name any that no longer describes what the code now does. This is the single largest class of review finding in this repository — a sentence the change itself falsified, left in place because nobody looked back at it.

2. Name anything your change left with nothing reaching it: a rule matching no element you emit, an export with no non-test importer, a branch now unreachable, a declaration the cascade discards.

3. For every resource your code reads, does it distinguish all THREE of never-asked, asked-and-found-nothing, and asked-and-FAILED? The third is the one that goes missing, and a failure rendered as an empty result reads as a confident zero. If a criterion named only two, say so — that is a finding about the plan, not a gap for you to fill silently.

4. For each `red_proof` you recorded, the failure output you pasted into `observed` has been written to `/run/media/capplequoppe/data/Repos/thai-script/plans/ai-conversation-practice/red-proofs/1.3.md`. READ THAT FILE rather than recalling it, and quote the line that decides it: name which of a real assertion failure, an import error, a build failure or a collection error each one shows. Only the first proves the test can catch the defect. Name any whose `observed` is empty — that is the weakest proof you can file, and the output is gone unless you still have it.

5. Is anything you wrote the ONLY one of its kind that lacks what its siblings have — the one status arm with no rule, the one title without a wrap, the one branch without a reason? Name it, or say the set is consistent.

**Finding nothing is a correct and expected answer.** Say so plainly if that is the case. Do not manufacture a finding to look thorough — a false one costs a fixer round to dismiss and teaches the next reader to skim these.

**One pass, and stay inside `covers`.** Repair what is yours and small; anything larger, or in a file you do not own, is REPORTED rather than fixed — the same rule that governs everything else you do. If you change anything, re-run the gates your task names and return your result again. If you change nothing, say that and stop.

---

**Deterministic lint over what you changed.** Compiled by code from your own diff — no model was asked anything, and every figure below was measured. It is ADVISORY: a violation does not block your task, and you may leave one and say why.

Re-check after a repair with `plan-runner macro run lint-changes`, which measures your changed set and nothing else. The report was rendered from `/run/media/capplequoppe/data/Repos/thai-script/plans/ai-conversation-practice/reports/lint/1.3.json`.

This is likely because the runner expects criterion ids matching a strict "AC" plus digits pattern, so ids like "AC8a"/"AC8b" with letter suffixes may not validate against the ac_tests schema properly.

This looks like a genuine plan/schema mismatch: the task declares AC8a and AC8b as criterion ids, but the id format only permits digits. I'll report this once as a user-decision finding, noting the file and symptom, and I still have the observed results for both in my transcript so nothing is lost.

Moving into the actual review, I'm starting with pass 1 — checking comments and docstrings adjacent to the changed lines. I recall the renderWithApp.tsx module docstring lists the environment repairs it registers (localStorage, Audio, canvas), but I added object-URL, MediaRecorder, and mediaDevices stubs without updating that docstring.

I'm confirming the remaining comments are still accurate — the pre-existing task 1.3 reference, StubMediaRecorder's docstring, the object-URL stub note about jsdom lacking create/revoke, the AppContext comment, HttpConversationPracticeClient's fetchJson docstring, toBase64's chunking rationale, the page docstring, and VERDICT_PRESENTATION's doc all check out. Now I'm scrutinizing the page's comment claiming one finished take maps to one judgement keyed on the blob's identity, verifying that against the actual effect dependencies.

Moving to a second pass, I'm now checking whether any exported utilities are unused — MIC_FIXTURE_MIME_TYPE, setMicPermission, StubMediaRecorder, StubConversationPracticePort, objectUrlCount, MicPermission, and CONVERSATION_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS all appear to have legitimate consumers.

content.text:
One pass done. **Two findings, both repaired**; the rest of the checks came back clean. Committed as `98ecb14`.

### 1. Stale adjacent prose — one found, fixed
`src/presentation/test-utils/renderWithApp.tsx`'s module docstring is an explicit enumeration of "the environment repairs every page-level render test needs" — `afterEach(cleanup)`, `localStorage`, `Audio`, canvas `getContext`. I added three more repairs to that exact `beforeEach` (`URL.createObjectURL`/`revokeObjectURL`, `MediaRecorder`, `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia`) and left the list describing the pre-change set. A list that claims to be exhaustive and silently isn't. Extended it with the two new bullets.

Everything else adjacent to a changed line I re-read and confirmed still true: `fetchJson`'s "every failure flattened to `null`" survives the simplification that removed `VERDICTS`; the page's "keyed on the blob's identity, so a re-render never re-submits" matches the effect's deps; the `AppContext.tsx` comment about constructing the client unconditionally is accurate.

### 2. Nothing reaching it — none
`CONVERSATION_BACKEND_BASE_URL` and `CONVERSATION_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` have no non-test importer, but the task required both as *named* constants ("base URL a module constant", "a named, generous deadline"), so naming them is the point rather than a leftover. `StubMediaRecorder` / `MIC_FIXTURE_MIME_TYPE` / `setMicPermission` / `MicPermission` / `StubConversationPracticePort` live in `test-utils`, whose only importers are tests by design. No unreachable branch, no discarded declaration.

### 3. Three states
**Judge result: all three present** — never-asked (`judgement === null`, record button), in-flight (`judging`), asked-and-**failed** (`{status:"unavailable"}` → its own alert), asked-and-answered. And the contract's `"unscored"` is a fourth thing again: the backend admitting it *couldn't* score, rendered as neither pass nor fail.

**Opening: only two states exist, and that is the contract's shape, not a hole I filled silently.** `GET /conversation/opening` in `docs/conversation-backend-api.md` returns the one fixed question or an error — there is no "asked, found nothing" response in phase 1. AC4 named only unavailable-vs-loaded for the same reason. Worth re-reading at phase 2, when the bank can legitimately have no entry for a learner's tier; that is a finding about the plan's phase-2 surface, not about this task.

### 4. Red-proof classification — read from the artefact
All ten blocks in `red-proofs/1.3.md` are **real assertion failures**. None is an import error, build failure or collection error; none is empty. Deciding lines:

| | deciding line | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | `AssertionError: expected 'http://localhost:8000/api/conversatio…' to be '…/conversation/op…'` + frame `…test.ts:54:15` | real assertion |
| AC2 | `AssertionError: … to deeply equal …` with `- "reply_audio_mime_type": "audio/webm;codecs=opus"` / `+ "audio/wav"` | real assertion |
| AC3 | `AssertionError: promise rejected "TypeError: Failed to fetch" instead of resolving` — the mutant's rejection surfacing *through* the `resolves` matcher, not at collection | real assertion |
| AC4 | `→ expected <button …(1)></button> to be null` | real assertion |
| AC5 | `→ expected [ '' ] to include 'blob:question-audio'` | real assertion |
| AC6 | `→ expected 'audio/wav' to be 'audio/webm;codecs=opus'` | real assertion |
| AC9 | `AssertionError: expected { status: 'ok', …(2) } to deeply equal { status: 'unavailable' }` with `+ "status": "ok"` | real assertion |
| AC10 | `AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality` (the `expect(settled).toBe(true)` line) | real assertion |
| AC11 | `→ expected 'The conversation backend is not runni…' to match /Microphone access needed/i` | real assertion |

**AC7 is the weak one, and I am calling it myself.** Its block has the `×` and `FAIL` lines naming that exact test and the frame `109| expect(rendered).toBeTruthy();` — so it is a genuine per-test failure, not a collection error — but the deciding line (`TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element with the text: /could not be scored/i`) was filtered out by my grep, and what stands in its place is a parenthetical *I wrote*. The artefact's own preamble says a proof block is the output as seen, not an account of it. That paraphrase should not be there and the verbatim line is gone.

**AC8a and AC8b are absent from the file entirely** — I filed 12 proofs, ten landed. See the orchestration note below. Restating the two observations while I still have them: AC8a, mutation = deleted the `/conversation` `<Route>` from `App.tsx`, observed a `TestingLibraryElementError` from the awaited `findByRole("heading", …)` at `App.test.tsx:37`; AC8b, mutation = replaced `new HttpConversationPracticeClient()` in `AppContext.tsx` with an object literal, observed `→ expected { …(2) } to be an instance of HttpConversationPracticeClient`. Both real assertion failures.

### 5. Odd one out — one found, fixed
Four arms in the page render after a take. Three carried `state === "stopped" &&`; `{judgement?.status === "ok" && …}` was the single one without it. Behaviourally identical (a judgement only ever exists while stopped, and `tryAgain` clears it before `reset()`), so it was inconsistency rather than a bug — but it is exactly the "one branch without the guard its siblings have" shape. Added the guard. All nine page tests plus the App route test and a `GamePage` regression re-run green.

### Orchestration (reported once, not fixed)
`plans/ai-conversation-practice/red-proofs/1.3.md` is missing AC8a/AC8b: the result schema's `criterion` field requires `"AC"` + digits, but `task-1.3-frontend-port-adapter-page.md` declares its criteria as `AC8a`/`AC8b`, so the runner dropped both entries silently. Same file, `reports/lint/1.3.json`: `lint-changes` reports `not measured … no grammar covers '.md' files (and 6 more) — 14 violations were measured before this and are not shown` — no grammar covers the file types this task changed, so my earlier `pass` for that gate was wrong and is corrected to `not-run` below.
